findings.obs_text: In 2Sa 13:32 and 2Sa 13:33 Jonadab, son of Shimeah and brother of David, speaks to the king against a view: that all the young men, the king's sons, are dead. He names Amnon as the one dead, Absalom as the one who purposed it, and Tamar his sister as the cause.

In Joh 20:15 the woman Mary takes Jesus, who speaks to her, for the gardener: the one supposed about is Jesus himself. In Joh 21:25 the writer supposes about the many things Jesus did and the books they would fill.
findings.grounds: Supposing him to be the gardener

findings.obs_text: Man and God are named together where the view is false or forbidden: in Act 17:29 God's offspring must not think the divine like an image of man's imagination, in Rom 2:3 the man who judges is asked whether he supposes he escapes God's judgment, in 1Ti 6:5 people depraved in mind imagine godliness is gain, and in Jam 1:7 the doubting person must not suppose he will receive from the Lord.
findings.grounds: an image formed by the art and imagination of man
